title: Compliance packs
description: Evidence for a named control framework: the checks McHarbor can run against a live host, the evidence it records, and the controls it cannot see.
disclaimer: A pack is evidence for a framework, not a claim of compliance with one. A passing check means the check passed — whether the control is met is your judgement and your auditor's.

framework.label: Framework
framework.mappingOnly: Evidence mapping only — this framework has no mechanical checks

actions.showFacts: Show the facts behind this verdict

runDialog.title: Run the checks now
runDialog.body: This reads the Docker daemon and every container on the selected environment and records a new run. It changes nothing on the host.

attestation.title: Sign-off
attestation.description: Who reviewed this evidence and accepted it, when, and on which run. A sign-off is never edited; a newer one supersedes it and both stay on record.
attestation.never: Nobody has signed off on this yet.
attestation.noRun: No run: a sign-off on the review as a whole
attestation.runOpen: The run is still in progress. Sign off once it has finished.

dialog.title: Record a sign-off
dialog.body: This records, under your name and the current time, that you reviewed the evidence below and accept it. It cannot be edited or deleted afterwards.
dialog.notePlaceholder: What you reviewed, what you accepted, and where the decision is recorded
dialog.noteRequired: A note is required: a sign-off without a word of justification is not evidence of a review.

toast.failed: The check run could not be started

table.empty: This pack has never been run, so no control carries a verdict yet.

notAssessed.title: Controls not assessed
notAssessed.body: {{count}} of this pack's controls carry no verdict. Not assessed is not a pass: it means the evidence could not be gathered, or McHarbor cannot see the control at all.

fact.interContainerCommunication: Inter-container communication on the default bridge

reason.daemonUnavailable: The Docker daemon could not be read, so this control has no verdict.
reason.containersUnavailable: The container list could not be read, so this control has no verdict.
reason.inspectIncomplete: Some containers could not be inspected, so a clean result would only describe the ones that were.
reason.containerListCapped: More containers exist than one run inspects, so this result covers a subset.
reason.noContainers: This environment has no containers, so there was nothing to check.
reason.notCoveredByMcHarbor: McHarbor cannot see this control. It is listed so the gap is visible rather than implied.
reason.evidencedNotChecked: McHarbor records the evidence for this control but does not judge it.
reason.versionRecorded: The running engine version is recorded. Whether it is current for this host is not something McHarbor can know.
reason.versionUnreported: The daemon did not report its version.
reason.iccEnabled: Containers on the default bridge can reach each other without a network being declared.
reason.bridgeUnreadable: The default bridge network could not be inspected.
reason.debugLoggingEnabled: The daemon runs with debug logging, which records request detail into the host journal.
reason.legacyStorageDriver: The daemon uses a storage driver the benchmark objects to.
reason.storageDriverUnreported: The daemon did not report its storage driver.
reason.daemonTCPNoTLS: The daemon is reached over plain TCP, so anybody who can reach the port can command it.
reason.connectionTypeUnknown: The environment's configured transport could not be read.
reason.usernsDisabled: User namespace remapping is off, so a container root is the host root.
reason.noAuthorizationPlugin: No authorization plugin decides daemon requests.
reason.loggingDriverLocal: Container output stays on the host. A sidecar that ships it elsewhere satisfies the intent and this check cannot see it.
reason.liveRestoreDisabled: Containers stop when the daemon does.
reason.seccompDisabled: The daemon's default seccomp profile is disabled.
reason.seccompUnreported: The daemon did not report a seccomp profile.
reason.experimentalEnabled: The daemon is an experimental build.
reason.swarmActive: Swarm mode is active. That is a finding only on a host that is not meant to orchestrate with it.
reason.containersAddCapabilities: Containers add kernel capabilities beyond the default set.
reason.containersPrivileged: Containers run privileged, which is equivalent to host root.
reason.containersOnPrivilegedPorts: Containers publish to a host port below 1024.
reason.containersShareHostNetwork: Containers share the host network namespace.
reason.containersWithoutMemoryLimit: Containers have no memory limit, so one can exhaust the host.
reason.containersWithoutCPULimit: Containers have no CPU shares or quota.
reason.containersWritableRootfs: Containers have a writable root filesystem.
reason.containersRestartUnbounded: Containers restart without a bounded attempt count.
reason.containersShareHostPID: Containers share the host process namespace.
reason.containersShareHostIPC: Containers share the host IPC namespace.
reason.containersExposeHostDevices: Containers are given a host device directly.
reason.containersSharedMountPropagation: Containers use shared mount propagation, which lets them write to the host mount tree.
reason.containersShareHostUTS: Containers share the host UTS namespace.
reason.containersWithoutPIDsLimit: Containers have no PIDs limit, so a fork bomb can exhaust the host.
reason.containersMountDockerSocket: Containers mount the Docker socket, which is equivalent to host root.
